A source whose first line is '@startdef' is flagged by UmlSource#isStartDef (core/UmlSource.java:288) and BlockUml#isStartDef (BlockUml.java:241-244); this port's dispatcher has no equivalent construct -- src/core/block-extractor.ts never recognises '@startdef' as its own block type, so it falls through to a generic refusal (engine=unknown, no 'Assumed diagram type' printed at all, unlike the class-refusal rows in this same cohort). The same unported '@startdef block' concept is already filed as a defect by routing-heuristic-repair's T9: .agent-notes/T9-includedef-definitions-container.md (see also TContext.java:687-709, BlockUmlBuilder.java:150-156).

PSystemListOpenIconicFactory (PSystemBuilder.java:151) renders the full Open Iconic icon catalog (openiconic/PSystemListOpenIconic.java) for the bare 'listopeniconic' line; unported alongside PSystemOpenIconicFactory's single-glyph mode.

PSystemSudokuFactory (PSystemBuilder.java:163) parses the digit grid and solves it via DLXEngine/SudokuDLX's dancing-links algorithm (sudoku/SudokuDLX.java) and renders the grid with GraphicsSudoku (sudoku/GraphicsSudoku.java); this whole solver-plus-renderer subsystem is unported.

The top-level 'stdlib <name>' directive is dead code upstream -- StdlibDiagramFactory's constructor unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (klimt/sprite/StdlibDiagramFactory.java:50) and its PSystemBuilder registration is commented out (PSystemBuilder.java:171) -- but a bare 'stdlib' line (no argument) still reaches a library-catalog listing page (confirmed by the rendered per-library 'Delivered by <source>' credit line matching preproc/Stdlib.java:327's format string); the exact triggering class was not pinned down further (a preprocessor-level listing, not one of PSystemBuilder's factories), but the feature is unported either way.

PSystemWelcomeFactory (PSystemBuilder.java:133, tried FIRST for every @startuml) returns a genuine non-error PSystemWelcome diagram whenever source.getTotalLineCount() == 2 (PSystemWelcomeFactory.java:52) -- true here once the lone comment line is stripped. This port's dispatcher has no 'trivial-content tutorial page' concept at all, so every plugin refuses the block and class's refusal draws the error sentinel where the jar drew a friendly tutorial.

state-commands.ts's rule 16 transition pre-filter (pattern /[<>]/, passes:['two']) matches ANY line containing '<' or '>' as a cheap gate for CommandLinkState/CommandLinkStateReverse (statediagram/command/CommandLinkStateCommon.java#isEligibleFor), then delegates the real check to parseTransitionLine. dispatchCommand (src/diagrams/state/parser.ts:135-144) treats a PATTERN match alone as 'this line is handled', regardless of whether execute() actually recognised it -- so on pass 'one' the rule matches but is pass-ineligible (no-op), and on pass 'two' parseTransitionLine correctly returns null (not a transition) and execute() also no-ops; either way the line is silently swallowed instead of falling through to fallbackOrRefuse (parser.ts:182-205), unlike upstream's real per-command candidate matching (command/PSystemCommandFactory.java:169-175, 'Syntax Error?'). Verified directly: statePlugin.parse() on any line containing a bare '<...>' token (with no real transition arrow) returns an empty, unrefused AST; matchAnnotationCommand and matchSpriteCommand both independently return null for the same line, ruling out the fallback matchers as the swallower.
